question: How should one remember pure consciousness as pervasive when the body is contemplated in light of knowable emptiness?
premises: The body is taken as the locus of contemplation.
Knowable emptiness provides the ablative ground for the next step.
Pure consciousness alone is to be recollected as pervasive.
inference: On contemplating the body in view of knowable emptiness, one is to remember pure consciousness as pervasive.
plain_english: When the body is contemplated, one should remember pure consciousness alone as pervasive, on the ground of the emptiness of the knowable.
